The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(1)+{f}^{′}(1)(x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $f(1)=3,$ and since ${f}^{′}(x)={x}^{2}(5x+1),$ we have

$$
{f}^{′}(1)=(1)^{2}(5\cdot 1+1)=6.
$$

So, the tangent line approximation is given by

$$
L(x)=3+6(x-1).
$$

Now, we can approximate $f(1.3)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=1.3.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1.3) & ≈L(1.3) \\  & =3+6(1.3-1) \\  & =3+6(0.3) \\  & =3+1.8 \\  & =4.8.\end{aligned}
$$
